name: Hyderabadi Khichdi
subtitle: loose rice and moong dal cooked with whole spices, the city's breakfast plate

ingredients.qty: 200g short or medium grain, rinsed till the water runs clear

ingredients.note: the dish is defined by it; oil gives a flatter result

prepNotes: Soak the rice and dal together for 20 minutes, then drain well. This is what gives the grains their soft, separate texture.
Hyderabadi khichdi is eaten with khatta and kheema, so it is deliberately mild. Resist the urge to load it with spice powders.
Measure the water precisely: this khichdi should be loose and grainy, not a porridge.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a pressure cooker and crackle the cumin, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, peppercorns and bay leaf for 40 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and fry over medium heat 8 minutes, until light golden.
steps.tip: Stop at light gold, not brown. Dark onion muddies the pale colour this dish is supposed to have.

steps.text: Add the ginger and green chillies and fry 1 minute.
Stir in the drained rice and dal and fry 3 minutes, until the grains look glossy and smell nutty.
steps.tip: Frying the grains in ghee before the water goes in is what keeps them separate rather than sticky.

steps.text: Add the turmeric, salt and 900ml water, and stir once.
Close the cooker and cook on medium for 2 whistles, then turn off the heat and let the pressure release naturally, about 10 minutes.
Open up and fluff with a fork. The grains should be soft and just holding their shape, with no free liquid at the bottom.
Rest covered 5 minutes, then serve hot with khichdi ka khatta and a spoon of extra ghee.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. It firms up cold; reheat with 3-4 tbsp hot water in a covered pan over low heat, breaking up lumps with a fork.
